obligations.summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III point 1 that have applied harmonised standards or common specifications must choose between the internal control procedure (Annex VI) or the quality management system and technical documentation assessment with a notified body (Annex VII).
exceptions: Where harmonised standards do not exist and common specifications are not available, the provider must follow Annex VII (no choice).
Where the provider has not applied, or only partially applied, the harmonised standard, the provider must follow Annex VII.
Where applicable common specifications exist but have not been applied, the provider must follow Annex VII.
Where a harmonised standard has been published with a restriction, Annex VII applies for the restricted part.

obligations.summary: Where the Annex VII conformity assessment procedure is required, providers may choose any notified body, except that where the high-risk AI system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or Union institutions/bodies/offices/agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority must act as the notified body.
exceptions: For systems intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or Union institutions/bodies/offices/agencies, the market surveillance authority referred to in Article 74(8) or (9) acts as notified body instead of a freely chosen one.

obligations.summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III points 2 to 8 must follow the internal control conformity assessment procedure set out in Annex VI, without involvement of a notified body.
exceptions: The Commission may adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to subject these systems to the Annex VII procedure instead.

obligations.summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I Section A must follow the conformity assessment procedure required by those legal acts, with the requirements of Section 2 of Chapter III forming part of that assessment.
exceptions: Where the applicable legal act allows the product manufacturer to opt out of third-party conformity assessment based on full application of harmonised standards, the manufacturer may exercise that option only if it has also applied harmonised standards or common specifications covering all Section 2 requirements.

Notified bodies notified under those legal acts may control compliance with Section 2 requirements, provided their compliance with Article 31(4), (5), (10) and (11) was assessed during their notification procedure.

obligations.summary: High-risk AI systems that have already undergone a conformity assessment must undergo a new conformity assessment procedure in the event of a substantial modification, regardless of whether the modified system will be further distributed or continues to be used by the current deployer.
exceptions: Changes to a high-risk AI system that continues to learn after being placed on the market or put into service, where those changes were predetermined by the provider at initial conformity assessment and documented in the technical documentation per Annex IV point 2(f), do not constitute a substantial modification and do not trigger a new conformity assessment.
